 Order

The writ petition has been filed to call for the records relating to the impugned order passed by the
2nd respondent, dated 22.09.2014

in his proceedings bearing Na.Ka.a 116/2009 which was received by the petitioner on 01.09.2015 and quash the same and to direct the respondents to pay the compensation amount for the Survey No.657/1 measuring 1 acre and 40 cents as per the order in LACMA No.60 of 2000, dated 06.12.2001 @ Rs.980/- per cent together with interest and solatium to the petitioner.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that the property measuring an extent of 2 acres 10 cents comprised in Survey No.657/1 of Kamudhi Village, Ramnad District was settled on the petitioner by her father under a registered settlement deed, dated 30.01.1978.
On 24.09.1990, Section _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4(1) notification under the Land Acquisition Act was notified proposing to acquire the lands.
Despite objections by the petitioner, Section 6 declaration was issued and award was passed on 05.03.1991.
The petitioner would submit that the copy of the award was not furnished to her and the compensation amount has also not been disbursed to her till date.
It is only in the year 2012, that the petitioner has approached the 2nd respondent and obtained the certified copy on 10.09.2012.
Thereafter, the petitioner made a representation to the 1st respondent to disburse the compensation amount as per the award, dated 05.03.1991.
Since the amount was not disbursed, she had renewed her request on 12.12.2012.
Thereafter, by communication, dated 17.01.2013, the 2nd respondent had informed that necessary steps would be taken for disbursement of the compensation amount.

After several exchanges, the 2nd respondent informed the petitioner by letter, dated 30.04.2013 that the amount due to the petitioner had been deposited in the Sub Treasury, Mudukulathur and the same has become time barred and therefore, only after getting appropriate permission, the compensation could be disbursed.

The petitioner is also aggrieved by the fact that the compensation in respect _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of an adjacent owner S.Nagoor Meera had been enhanced to a sum of Rs. 980/- per cent by the Sub Court,
Paramakudi in L.A.C.M.A.No.60 of 2000 by its order, dated 06.12.2001.
The petitioner would submit that she is also therefore entitled to the same amount.
Therefore, she has come forward with the writ petition.

3. When the matter had come up on 06.08.2024, this Court had directed the learned Additional Government Pleader to report to the Court as to what is the stage of the deposit of the compensation amount.

Today, when the matter was called, the files were produced and it is seen that as early as on 22.03.1991, a sum of Rs.7,792/- has been deposited under the head of revenue deposit, since the petitioner had refused to receive the amount.
This fact is also been communicated to the petitioner by the 2nd respondent vide his memo (Fwpg;ghiz), dated 31.12.2014.

sentences.text: The records would indicate that the petitioner though dissatisfied with the compensation, had not taken any steps to have the matter referred under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.
The ____
_ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that even without resorting to the provisions of Section 18, under Section 28 A, the petitioner was entitled to the same amount as given to the neighbouring land owner.
5.
However, a perusal of the provision clearly shows that in order to claim the same, written application has to be given to the Collector within 3 months from the date of award passed by the Court.
The proviso to the Section would state that the time taken from the date of the award till the receipt of the award copy would stand excluded for calculating the aforesaid period of 3 months.
Under sub-section (2), the Collector is required to conduct an enquiry after giving notice to all the persons interested and giving them a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

Admittedly, in the instant case, no such application has been taken by the petitioner to date and even in the year 2012,
when the first move has been made by the petitioner, it is only a representation that she has made to the 2nd respondent.
Even the remedy under Section 28A of the Act has not been initiated by the petitioner.

In these circumstances, the petitioner _________ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis would only be entitled to a sum of Rs.7,792/- (Rupees Seven Thousand Seven Hundred and Ninety Two only) which had been deposited by the respondents.

Therefore, taking note of the fact that the time has long expired from the date of deposit, direction is issued to the 2nd respondent to disburse the said sum of Rs.7,792/- (Rupees Seven Thousand Seven Hundred and Ninety Two only) to the petitioner on or before 20.09.2024.
6.
With the above direction, this Writ Petition stands allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.

7. Post this case for reporting compliance on 23.09.2024.
